_readme: Where each string appears, and what a translator must know before touching it. voice: 'metaphor' or 'humour' means recreate the idea, never translate the sentence — if the image has no local equivalent, propose a replacement and flag it rather than rendering it literally. These are the strings that must never reach a machine-translation queue unflagged.

meta.title.note: Under 60 characters or search results truncate it.

nav.contact.note: Also the hero call to action. Plain verb, no urgency theatre.

nav.skipToContent.note: Must be translated: it is the first thing a keyboard user meets.

lang.en.note: ENDONYM. 'English' stays English in every locale, 'Deutsch' stays German. Never translate an endonym, never use a flag: a flag is a country, not a language.

lang.changed.where: live region, announced when the locale changes
lang.changed.note: Announced by a screen reader, so it is written in the language being switched TO.

meta.separator.where: page <title>, between the page name and the site name
meta.separator.note: TYPOGRAPHY, not copy. Decided by the locale's rules and pre-filled for every locale: en takes the em dash, de the spaced en dash. Not a string for a translator to improvise.

banner.eaa.note: Date in long European form. Never numeric.

hero.headline.note: Berlin is the studio's actual city — keep it, it is not decoration.

eaa.doorLine.where: end of the EAA intro section
eaa.doorLine.note: The door metaphor, and one of the two the tone doc names. Recreate the idea in the target language rather than translating the words. A German version must not become a rhetorical question if that reads as advertising — dry statement is safer.

a11y.houseLine.note: The house-and-door image. Same instruction as eaa.doorLine: recreate, don't translate.

a11y.captions.note: Dry list of everyday moments. The humour is in the recognition, not in any joke — if a locale's version needs a wink, cut it.

a11y.curbCuts.note: 'Curb cut' is a term of art in accessibility (Bordsteinabsenkung). Use the local term, not a description.

legal.body.note: BFSG, European Accessibility Act and Equality Act 2010 are official names — see glossary.md. Never translate them.

legal.standard.note: WCAG 2.1 Level AA is what EN 301 549 currently adopts. Do not 'update' it to 2.2 without checking which version the law cites.

legal.enforcement.note: Deliberately does NOT name a fine amount. The tone doc bans fear-based urgency, and the German brief singles out fear-selling as the sharpest difference from competitors. Do not reintroduce a number here.

who.motorDesc.note: Everyday situations, not medical conditions. Keep them ordinary.

what.perceivableTerm.note: The four WCAG principles. Use the W3C Authorized Translation's terms where one exists — for German: Wahrnehmbar, Bedienbar, Verständlich, Robust.

apply.exemption.note: {threshold} is formatted by Intl.NumberFormat as EUR in the locale's own convention — €2,000,000 in en, 2.000.000 € in de. Never hard-code the symbol or its position.

services.doorMetaphor.note: IMPERIAL MEASUREMENT. {height} is 5'10" in en and MUST be a metric height in every other locale — 1,78 m in de. The German brief says never carry an imperial measurement into a German sentence. The build supplies the value per locale; a translator must not hard-code it.

approach.futureProofTerm.note: Was 'Future-proof' — changed because the tone doc lists it as marketing fluff. Keep the replacement plain in every locale.

magnifier.toggle.note: 1.5× uses the multiplication sign, not the letter x.

magnifier.close.note: An accessible name — invisible, and still governed by the voice rules.
